updated_content: Bare-metal: single loop, no OS scheduler; appropriate when the workload is bounded and deterministic, because the developer controls task ordering and there is no scheduler-induced overhead or jitter. RTOS: preemptive multitasking with scheduling guarantees; necessary when the system must multiplex tasks with bounded worst-case latency, priority inversion handling, and deadline-aware dispatch — but the scheduler itself introduces determinism trade-offs such as context-switch cost, priority inversion risk, and tick-timer dependency that bare-metal systems avoid entirely.
